analysis: Market regime is UPTREND (SPY +3.2% vs SMA50, positive slope) — a supportive backdrop, but selectivity still matters. Portfolio review: (1) A (Agilent) has earnings in 20 days (Aug 26) — the position is up 8.79% and thesis is intact, but near-term binary risk is real; I recommend setting a mental stop just below the Aug earnings gap and being prepared to trim if the stock gaps down on results. Not a forced sell — the quality case holds. (2) AMP, LMT, MCO all tracking trend quietly with no thesis breaks. Portfolio heat is very low at 1.51%, deployment at 75%, and there is ~$19.9k headroom for one additional position. Among the 30 screened candidates, most are either extended (TRV, NSC, NDAQ, TROW all above 75% of 52-week range), mixed-trend with a declining SMA50 (TYL, CTSH, NOC, HSY), or face near-term earnings risk (JKHY in 12 days, ULTA in 21 days). One genuinely asymmetric setup stands out: PGR (Progressive) is resting almost exactly at its SMA50 (+0.7%) in a confirmed uptrend, sitting at 48% of 52-week range, with best-in-class insurance fundamentals. A tight ATR of 2.6% allows a properly sized position within the remaining headroom. One trade proposed; no forced additions beyond that.

trades.entry_strategy: Limit order at $212.50 or better, ideally on a pullback to or just above the SMA50 (~$211). Do not chase above $215.
trades.rationale: FUNDAMENTAL: Progressive is arguably the best-run personal auto insurer in the US. ROE of 34.9%, P/E of 10.68 trailing (13.06 fwd), and $15.1B in FCF reflect a structural cost and pricing advantage driven by Snapshot telematics and disciplined underwriting. Revenue growth 7.3% YoY with analyst EPS revisions trending higher (+0.4%). Insurance is benefiting from a hard pricing cycle and Progressive is the clear share-gainer. TECHNICAL: Price is in a confirmed UPTREND, sitting only +0.7% above its rising SMA50 (slope +3.1%), at 48% of 52-week range — classic Stage 1-to-2 basing territory. This is a low-risk entry point against a defined support level rather than a momentum chase. ATR of 2.6% is among the tightest in the candidate set, enabling a properly sized position with a 2x ATR stop at $201.70 (5.2% below entry). Earnings are 69 days out (Oct 14), well outside the near-term noise window.
trades.exit_plan: Exit if: (1) price closes below stop $201.70 (thesis invalidated technically); (2) combined ratio deterioration signals underwriting discipline breaking down; (3) broader market turns confirmed downtrend; (4) stock reaches $235 target (reassess thesis at that point for LTCG hold extension); (5) time stop — if no meaningful progress within 90 days, review allocation against opportunity cost.
